title: Stable influence of the odd part
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $i$ be a coordinate. Define the odd part of $f$ by $f_{\\mathrm{odd}}(x)=(f(x)-f(-x))/2$. For every $\\rho\\in[0,1]$, the stable influence of $f_{\\mathrm{odd}}$ at parameter $\\rho$ and coordinate $i$ is at most the stable influence of $f$ there.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
